answer: At the dawn of each billing period, a registry binds one agent identity to a unique mobile number that the carrier confirms by silent authentication, rejecting duplicates. An attacker's voyage to create n sybils requires n live SIM subscriptions, each paying a recurring fee in that same period; profit is n(R-C), positive only while per-period reward exceeds the cheapest plan fee. A pearl of caution: bulk SIM markets weaken the bound unless the protocol caps per-period reward below that marginal fee, and carrier collusion remains unenforced.
